definition: A learning room where students use materials or equipment independently.
example: The self-access lab has recordings for pronunciation practice.

definition: A manager with substantial responsibility and authority.
example: A senior manager must approve purchases above the spending limit.

definition: A feeling of having achieved something worthwhile.
example: Completing the first five kilometres gave her a sense of success.

definition: To save part of one's money for a particular purpose or future need.
example: I set money aside each month for unexpected repairs.

definition: To cut the wool from sheep.
example: The farmer will shear the sheep before the summer heat arrives.

definition: A person responsible for running a shop.
example: The shop manager arranged extra staff for the weekend sale.

definition: One individual object or unit.
example: Passengers may carry a single item of hand luggage.

definition: Fabric that is silver in colour or contains silver-coloured threads.
example: The designer used silver cloth for the costume's collar.
usage: The wording alone does not establish that the material contains real silver.

definition: A small mark left by a healed injury on a man's chin.
example: The witness described a man with a small scar on his chin.

definition: Effects connected with social issues or conditions.
example: The report examines the effects of social conditions on children's health.
usage: Social matter effects is nonstandard and its intended meaning is uncertain; effects of social issues is one possible interpretation.

definition: Extra socks kept for use when another pair is wet, dirty, or unavailable.
example: Pack spare socks in case your feet get wet on the hike.

definition: Mail sent or handled using a service beyond ordinary delivery.
example: Ask whether special mail needs a signature on delivery.
usage: This is a broad, context-dependent phrase; registered mail or express mail may be the precise service intended.

definition: A rule that applies to a particular situation or group.
example: A special rule allows young children to enter free of charge.

definition: A museum focused on a particular subject or type of object.
example: The town has a specialized museum devoted to historic clocks.

definition: Distinct biological kinds of crocodiles.
example: The guide explained how two species of crocodiles differ in size.

definition: A notebook whose pages are held together by a coiled wire or plastic binding.
example: She takes lecture notes in a spiral notebook.

definition: Shoes designed for exercise or sporting activities.
example: Wear sports shoes with good grip for the indoor training session.

definition: A suite offered as a property's ordinary category of connected rooms.
example: We booked a standard suite with a bedroom and a sitting area.
usage: Suite categories and facilities vary by property.

definition: Steel and timber considered together as building or manufacturing materials.
example: The bridge uses steel and wood in its structure.

definition: An area or amount of room available for keeping things.
example: The flat has storage space under the stairs.

definition: The amounts of pressure, worry, or tension experienced.
example: The survey found higher stress levels during the examination period.

definition: Firm limits or close supervision over an activity or process.
example: The laboratory keeps strict control over access to dangerous chemicals.

definition: An account designed or provided for a student, such as a bank or online account.
example: My student account has no monthly banking fee.
usage: The type of account depends on the context.

definition: A building providing accommodation for students, often with shared facilities.
example: The student hostel is a ten-minute walk from campus.

definition: Help or facilities provided for students.
example: The student service helps new arrivals find accommodation.
usage: Student services is usual for the institution's wider set of support functions.

definition: A group whose members meet to study or support one another's learning.
example: Our study club meets every Thursday to revise lecture notes.

definition: Things kept inside a purse.
example: She emptied the contents of her purse to look for the missing key.
usage: Stuff of purse is nonstandard; contents of a purse is the natural form.

definition: To send or hand in a document for consideration or processing.
example: Please submit the document before the application deadline.

definition: Assistance provided to help people use something or deal with a difficulty.
example: The support service helped me reset my university password.

definition: A written account presenting the main points of a larger body of information.
example: The summary report highlights the survey's three main findings.

definition: A course teaching skills for staying alive in difficult conditions.
example: The survival course taught us how to find safe drinking water.

definition: To measure the pressure of blood circulating through a person's arteries.
example: The nurse will take your blood pressure before the consultation.

definition: To do things that involve a possibility of loss, failure, or harm.
example: Entrepreneurs often have to take risks when starting a business.

definition: A group whose members meet to discuss or practise teaching.
example: The teaching club meets monthly to exchange classroom activities.
usage: This descriptive name does not specify a formal type of organization.

definition: The people employed to teach at an institution.
example: The teaching staff attended a workshop on assessment.

definition: A survey conducted by asking questions over the phone.
example: The researchers used a telephone survey to interview residents.

definition: Heat originating within the Earth.
example: The plant uses terrestrial heat to generate electricity.
usage: Geothermal heat is the more usual technical term.

definition: The part of an organization responsible for promoting its products or services.
example: The marketing department designed the new advertising campaign.

definition: People who have little money or few financial resources.
example: The charity provides winter clothing for the poor.
usage: A collective expression with plural agreement; people living in poverty can be more specific.

definition: The main topic or central idea of a project.
example: The theme of the project is sustainable transport.
usage: Normally say theme of a project or the project's theme.

definition: Sections of a book or thesis that explain theoretical ideas.
example: The theory chapters explain the models used in the analysis.

definition: Land whose soil has been turned or prepared for growing crops.
example: Heavy rain washed soil from the newly tilled land.

definition: A recurring way of reasoning or organizing thoughts.
example: The exercise asks you to notice a thinking pattern that leads to worry.

definition: The name given to an essay.
example: Write the title of the essay at the top of the first page.
usage: Use title of an essay or the essay's title.

definition: More tasks or effort than can comfortably be managed.
example: She had too much work to finish everything before the weekend.

definition: Printed booklets giving visitors information about places and activities.
example: The reception desk has tourist brochures with maps of the old town.

definition: Rules governing how people and vehicles use roads.
example: Drivers must follow traffic rules even when the roads are quiet.

definition: A set of travel services sold together, often including transport and accommodation.
example: The travel package includes flights, hotel accommodation, and airport transfers.

definition: A college name shared by several educational institutions.
example: Check which Trinity College the application form refers to.
usage: The name alone does not identify a particular college or its location.

definition: A television programme in which a host talks with guests.
example: The actor discussed her new film on a TV chat show.

definition: A place below ground level where cars can be parked.
example: The hotel has an underground car park beneath the main building.

definition: A street name consisting of University and Drive.
example: The taxi driver asked which building on University Drive we needed.
usage: The name alone does not identify a particular street.

definition: An Australian university named after the city of Wollongong.
example: She is applying to the University of Wollongong for postgraduate study.

definition: A general movement toward higher values or amounts.
example: The graph shows an upward trend in electricity demand.

term: vary according to the type, shape
definition: To differ depending on category or shape.
example: Delivery charges vary according to the type and shape of the parcel.
usage: The original is incomplete; specify what varies and join type and shape with and.

definition: A planned piece of work involving the creation or use of video.
example: Our video project documents changes along the riverbank.

definition: A class or service category offering special treatment to selected customers.
example: The airline advertises a VIP class with additional lounge access.
usage: VIP means very important person; the exact service and whether it is a travel category depend on the provider.

definition: Fine particles released by a volcanic eruption.
example: Volcanic dust reduced visibility near the mountain.
usage: Volcanic ash is the usual technical term for fine fragments of erupted rock and glass.

definition: A group that organizes walks for its members.
example: The walking club meets at the station every Sunday morning.

definition: The collection, movement, storage, or treatment of discarded material.
example: Workers receive training in safe waste handling.

definition: Supplies of water available for use by people or ecosystems.
example: The drought placed pressure on the region's water resources.

definition: A social event held to greet new arrivals.
example: The department organized a welcome party for first-year students.

definition: Writing across a broad space, or writing with broadly spaced characters.
example: The large, widely spaced handwriting was easy to read from a distance.
usage: Wide writing is nonstandard and ambiguous; wide reading may be a transcription error, but cannot be assumed.

definition: The planned shape and structure of an aircraft's wing.
example: Engineers tested a new wing design in the wind tunnel.

term: wood should be cut and seasoned
definition: Timber needs to be cut and dried or conditioned before use.
example: Wood should be cut and seasoned before it is used to make furniture.

definition: To carry out tasks in an organized and methodical way.
example: Work systematically through the checklist so you do not miss a step.

definition: The diplomatic office representing your country in another country.
example: If you lose your passport abroad, contact your own embassy.

definition: To make a strong effort to do something.
example: I will try hard to improve my listening score before the next test.

definition: On a greater number of occasions.
example: The buses run more often during the morning rush hour.

definition: To focus one's work or study on a particular subject or activity.
example: The clinic specializes in sports injuries.

definition: The colour of the hair on a person's head.
example: The form asks for height, eye colour, and hair color.
usage: Color is American spelling; colour is British spelling.

definition: Hair arranged in curves or waves.
example: She had waved hair styled carefully for the ceremony.
usage: Waved can mean deliberately styled into waves; wavy hair describes the texture more generally.

definition: Hair gathered and tied at the back of the head, hanging like a tail.
example: She tied her hair in a ponytail before going for a run.
usage: The usual spelling is ponytail.

definition: Having spectacles on one's face.
example: The man wearing glasses is our new lecturer.

definition: A shirt patterned with squares of different colours.
example: He wore a blue checked shirt and dark trousers.

definition: To lack information about something.
example: We were in the dark about the change of venue.
usage: The idiomatic form is be in the dark; without the article, the original is incomplete.

definition: The identifying number printed in a passport.
example: Enter your passport number exactly as it appears on the document.

definition: The food a person likes most.
example: My favourite food is vegetable lasagne.

definition: The ability to understand and use English effectively.
example: The university requires evidence of English proficiency.

definition: A telephone number used to contact someone at home.
example: Please leave your home number in case we need to contact you.
usage: Home telephone number is clearer; the phrase can have other meanings in specialized contexts.

definition: The calendar day on which a journey or departure begins.
example: The ticket shows the date of departure as 18 June.

definition: A person who organizes accommodation arrangements.
example: The housing coordinator helped us find a room near campus.

definition: Available to rent under a lease agreement.
example: The sign says the shop premises are for lease.

definition: An identifying number assigned to a room.
example: Write your room number on the breakfast order form.

definition: A bedroom intended for one occupant or containing one single bed.
example: The flat has a single bedroom suitable for one student.
usage: Single room may describe occupancy, while single bedroom can also contrast with double bedroom.

definition: Cooking appliances that use electricity to heat food.
example: The accommodation has electric stoves in the shared kitchen.

definition: A label placed on a vehicle to show permission to park.
example: Display your parking sticker on the windscreen.

definition: To attach a locking device to a vehicle's wheel so it cannot move.
example: Officials may clamp the wheel of a car parked without permission.

definition: To arrange in advance for something such as a table, seat, or room to be kept for you.
example: We need to make a reservation for six people at the restaurant.

definition: To arrange in advance to use a room.
example: I would like to book a room for two nights.

definition: A travel ticket without a fixed travel date or with flexible arrangements.
example: Ask whether the open ticket requires advance seat booking.
usage: Conditions depend on the transport provider; an open ticket does not necessarily guarantee a seat.

definition: A shop selling eligible goods without certain local taxes or duties.
example: She bought perfume at the airport duty-free shop.

definition: Having no available places or rooms because all have been reserved.
example: The hotel is fully booked for the festival weekend.
usage: Fulling-booked is a spelling error; use fully booked.

definition: To reserve a particular room in advance.
example: Please book the room with the sea view for our anniversary.

definition: Regions with many hills.
example: Cycling is more demanding in hilly areas.

definition: A leisure journey by boat along a river.
example: The river cruise passes the old castle before returning to the quay.

definition: To take money out of a bank account.
example: You can withdraw money from the cash machine outside the library.

definition: To set up a bank account intended for students.
example: Bring proof of enrolment when you open a student account.

definition: To exchange money in pounds for money in dollars.
example: I need to change pounds into dollars before my trip.

definition: To formally ask to be considered for employment.
example: She decided to apply for a job at the museum.

definition: Money received in addition to ordinary wages.
example: Staff receive extra pay for working on public holidays.

definition: To monitor the supply of goods held for sale or use.
example: Keep an eye on stock so we can reorder before the shelves are empty.

definition: To ask for a doctor to come and provide medical help.
example: The hotel manager had to send for a doctor when a guest became ill.

definition: To have liquid mucus flowing from the nose.
example: I have a runny nose and keep needing tissues.

definition: To have a nose blocked by congestion.
example: I have a stuffed nose and cannot breathe comfortably through it.
usage: Have a stuffy nose or have a blocked nose is more conventional.

definition: An injection given to help prevent an illness, often a vaccine.
example: The clinic offers a preventive injection against influenza.
usage: Vaccination is usually more precise when a vaccine is meant.

definition: The most important area of business or production in a place.
example: Tourism is the town's main industry.

definition: The process of producing wine, usually by fermenting grapes.
example: The course explains the role of yeast in wine-making.

definition: The minimum recorded or expected temperature.
example: The lowest temperature tonight is expected to be minus two degrees.

definition: Having existed for a long time and containing moisture.
example: The old and wet wooden boards needed replacing.
usage: This is a literal combination of adjectives; cold and wet may be a transcription error in weather contexts, but cannot be assumed.

definition: Located across from something, or contrasting strongly with it.
example: His answer was opposite to what I had expected.
usage: For a location, directly opposite the station is usually more natural than opposite to the station.

definition: To cross directly to the other side without turning.
example: Go straight across the road and enter the building with the red door.

definition: To travel in an easterly direction.
example: Go east for two kilometres, then turn toward the lake.

definition: To follow a route until reaching a stated place or point.
example: Go along this street till you reach the post office.
usage: The dots mark slots for a route and an endpoint; until is a more formal alternative to till.

definition: To be located at the first road or turn on the left.
example: The road to the museum is the first left after the bridge.
usage: Use take the first left for an instruction; be the first left describes which turning is meant.

term: be on the corner of A street and B street
definition: To be situated where two named streets meet.
example: The bank is on the corner of King Street and Market Street.
usage: A street and B street are placeholders for real street names.

definition: Facilities or routes that allow wheelchair users to enter and move through a place.
example: The museum provides wheelchair access through its side entrance.
usage: Wheelchair is normally written as one word.

definition: The country consisting of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
example: The United Kingdom uses the pound sterling as its currency.

definition: A meeting introducing new people to an institution, role, or setting.
example: The orientation meeting explains how to use the library and student portal.

definition: Active involvement in class activities or discussions.
example: Class participation counts toward the final course mark.

definition: Kept in a restricted library reserve collection rather than on freely accessible shelves.
example: Ask a librarian for items held in the closed reserve collection.
usage: Closed reserved is nonstandard; closed reserve is a plausible library interpretation, but the exact original meaning is uncertain.

definition: A printer that forms characters and images using small pins that strike an inked ribbon.
example: The old dot-matrix printer is still used for multi-part invoices.

definition: Legal rules governing rights over the copying and use of creative works.
example: Copyright laws may limit how much of a textbook you can photocopy.

definition: An exercise or task in which missing words or information are supplied.
example: The listening test includes gap filling in a short summary.

definition: A person's own view, especially one not expressed publicly.
example: My private opinion differs from the statement issued by the committee.

definition: An office that manages an organization's routine operations and records.
example: Submit the completed form to the administration office.
usage: Administration office or administrative office is more conventional than administrating office.

definition: The amount of something contained in one jar.
example: I bought a jar of honey at the market.

definition: An unnecessary or unproductive use of something.
example: Waiting for the wrong bus was a waste of time.

definition: A large amount of something.
example: The repairs required a great deal of patience.
usage: Normally followed by an uncountable noun.

definition: Several different kinds or examples of something.
example: The library offers a range of online resources.

definition: At an unspecified point in a process or period.
example: At some stage, we will need to replace the old computers.

definition: To be joined or fastened to something.
example: The label is attached to the outside of the box.
usage: The phrase can also describe emotional affection; the physical sense is used here.

definition: To know something through experience or previous contact.
example: You should be familiar with the emergency procedures before using the lab.

definition: To be better in quality, ability, or performance than something else.
example: This material is superior to the cheaper alternative in durability.

definition: To provide what a person or group needs.
example: The cafeteria caters for students with different dietary requirements.

definition: To study a course leading to a university degree.
example: She wants to do a degree in environmental science.
usage: Common in British English; study for a degree is another option.

definition: At stated rates of movement or operation.
example: These trains travel at speeds of up to two hundred kilometres an hour.

definition: To be combined or linked with something.
example: Heavy rain was coupled with strong winds during the storm.

definition: To have something else put in one's place.
example: The broken chairs will be replaced with new ones.

definition: To be responsible for a problem or bad outcome.
example: Poor maintenance was to blame for the equipment failure.

definition: To spend time painting pictures or surfaces.
example: We do some painting in the art room on Friday afternoons.
usage: Do some painting or paint is usually more natural.

definition: To register as a participant in a course.
example: You can enrol on the evening course through the college website.
usage: Enrol is British spelling; enroll is American spelling. Enrol in is also used.

definition: Starting at the earliest point of an event or process.
example: The instructions were clear from the very beginning.

definition: To get or drink a coffee, often quickly or informally.
example: Let's grab a coffee before the next lecture.

definition: From another country.
example: Many of the conference speakers have travelled from abroad.

definition: To treat something as more important or deal with it before other things.
example: The council will give priority to urgent housing repairs.

definition: To argue with someone or speak angrily to them.
example: She had words with her neighbour about the loud music.
usage: Sb. stands for somebody; have a word with someone usually means a brief conversation instead.

definition: Working for a particular employer.
example: He had three assistants in his employ.
usage: A formal or somewhat old-fashioned expression.

definition: To plan or mean to do something.
example: I intend to submit the application before Friday.

definition: To formally request money, compensation, or another entitlement.
example: You can make a claim on your insurance after the theft.
usage: The phrase can also mean asserting that something is true; the insurance sense is used here.

definition: To achieve a specified goal or required level.
example: The sales team worked together to meet its monthly target.

definition: To ask someone for ideas, knowledge, or advice.
example: Could I pick your brain about choosing a research topic?
usage: Informal; one's is replaced by the person whose advice is sought.

definition: Under the particular circumstances being discussed.
example: The bus has been cancelled; in this case, we should take a taxi.

definition: To formally request something by submitting required information.
example: You must make an application before you can receive the grant.

definition: To help people learn about and understand an issue.
example: The campaign will raise public awareness of food waste.

definition: To perform a useful function or fulfil a need.
example: The spare room serves a purpose as a quiet study space.

definition: To participate in an activity or event.
example: All students are invited to take part in the sports day.

definition: To express the same idea using different words.
example: To put it another way, every participant must finish all three tasks.

definition: To introduce styles or behaviours that other people begin to follow.
example: Popular designers often set trends in fashion.

definition: To create an image using a camera.
example: May I take a photograph of the display?
usage: Use take a photograph or take photographs; photograph needs a determiner when singular.

definition: To be carried by water onto a shore or other surface.
example: Plastic bottles sometimes wash up onto the beach after a storm.

definition: An organized trip undertaken to explore or carry out work underwater.
example: The diving expedition surveyed the reef for damaged coral.

definition: A sightseeing journey made by bus.
example: The bus tour stops at the castle and the harbour.

definition: Purchases or offers that provide good value.
example: We found good deals on winter coats in the sale.

definition: A cinema experience using images displayed around viewers through a full circle.
example: The museum's 360-degree cinema surrounds visitors with images of the rainforest.
usage: Three-sixty is an informal reading of 360; 360-degree cinema is the clearer written form. The original venue is not identified.

definition: The goal that gives a team the score needed to win a match.
example: She scored the winning goal in the last minute of the game.

definition: The ability to understand where objects or people are in relation to oneself and one another.
example: Parking a car in a narrow space requires spatial awareness.

definition: Written or recorded materials from the past used as evidence about events or lives.
example: The archive preserves historical documents, including letters and land records.
